newsitem.title: USA: Belo sells Health Network to Columbia/HCA.
newsitem.headline: Belo sells Health Network to Columbia/HCA.

text.p: A.H. Belo Corp said Tuesday it has an agreement in principle to sell substantially all its interest in America's Health Network, giving Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp a majority interest in the 24-hour health news cable channel.
Terms were not disclosed, and calls to the Belo offices in Dallas and Columbia/HCA's offices Tuesday evening were not immediately answered.

America's Health Network was launched in March 1996 by The Providence Journal Co, which Belo acquired in February. The cable channel is available to more than six million basic cable television and direct broadcast satellite subscribers in the United States.
"As the nation's largest health care company, Columbia is ideally positioned to support AHN's continued growth," Columbia/HCA said in a statement.
Belo owns and operates 16 network-affiliated television stations; six daily newspapers; three local or regional cable news channels and Belo Productions Inc.
Belo said the sale is part of its effort to restructure its interest in America's Health Network.
